title: Suchbot
subtitle: An agent practice built around a shared document graph.
overview: Suchbot is the public face of my ongoing work with Hermes: research, publishing, and creative tools people can use in the Farcaster timeline. Behind it is a larger experiment in giving an agent useful context and improving its behavior through daily use.
knowledge: Logseq is the document graph. Its linked pages and blocks let me organize the notes that my agent and I work from. I initiated logseqd, a Clojure/DataScript service that makes that graph queryable by the agent and other tools, then added a mobile interface for capture and review.
feedback: Feedback becomes part of the system. Repeated writing corrections became a mechanical check before publication. Public interactions can consult explicitly published pages; a server-side gate keeps private documents out of that access path.
contribution: My role: I initiated the project, set the workflow and interface requirements, and tested it in daily use. Hermes contributed substantially to implementation.
decisions: A service around existing notes, rather than a separate knowledge silo. A mobile interface for quick capture. Journal upkeep shaped around conversation, because that’s how I naturally work.
role: I initiated logseqd, set the workflow and interface requirements, and tested the system in daily use. Hermes contributed substantially to implementation.
limitations: A small, self-hosted system with ongoing maintenance. Logseq syntax, indexing, and mobile caching required iteration. The public template is an untested alpha; it is not a finished enterprise product.
